children: Gold prices hover around $4,400 a troy ounce as investors await the release of key U.S. inflation data ahead of the Federal Reserve's policy meeting next week. "Higher Treasury yields remain a headwind after a planned U.S. government purchase of up to $6 billion of longer-dated debt failed to materially lower borrowing costs, while Brent's move above $100 a barrel has reinforced concerns that Middle East-driven energy inflation could keep price pressures elevated," says Soojin Kim from MUFG. According to the CME Group's FedWatch tool, traders are now pricing in a 60% probability of a rate hike this month. In early European trading, New York gold futures are flat at $4,458.40 an ounce. (giulia.petroni@wsj.com)
